column1: Broaden PATCH /auth/me beyond owner-only
column8: RESOLVED: PATCH /auth/me now accepts all 4 roles. Real scoping finding, not a simple permission swap: manager/admin/registered_user have no profile table in Postgres at all (location_manager.user_id is a bare Cognito sub, not a FK, by design) -- editing their name/phone would mean a Cognito-attribute edit from the frontend, not a backend DB write. Rather than inventing a table, non-owner roles now get an honest 404 (code: no_editable_profile) instead of a wrongful 403. Owner's write also now lazily provisions owner_account itself (previously a require_owner side effect). Also fixed in the same PR: update_me was writing zero audit_log entries -- a pre-existing violation of root CLAUDE.md's audit_log requirement, caught during self-review.

column1: Fix: cached async DB engine reused across event loops on a warm management-command container
column8: Found live 2026-09-18 running the real 26-restaurant Irving CSV import: a 2-row test batch succeeded, then the full 26-row batch errored on row 0 only ("Task ... got Future ... attached to a different loop") while the other 25 rows succeeded normally in the same invocation -- reproduced twice, always on a batch's first row. Root cause: app/db/session.py's `_engine`/`_session_factory` are module-level globals, cached across warm Lambda invocations by design (cold-start-only, correct for the FastAPI/Mangum HTTP path, which keeps one event loop alive for the container's life) -- but every management command (app/scripts/management.py) wraps its DB work in its own `asyncio.run(...)`, a fresh event loop every invocation. A warm container reusing the cached engine across two such invocations hands the second one an engine whose asyncpg connection pool is still bound to the first invocation's now-closed loop; the first DB operation on the new loop fails this way, later operations succeed once the pool reconnects under the current loop. Fixed: new `dispose_engine()` (app/db/session.py) disposes the engine and resets both globals -- called from inside the SAME event loop the engine was used under (a `finally` at the end of each management command's own DB-touching coroutine), never from a later/different loop, which would hit the identical bug during disposal itself. All four DB-touching management commands (seed_dev_data, bulk_import_restaurants JSON + CSV paths, delete_user_data) now do this; alembic_upgrade is unaffected -- it uses a separate, non-cached engine. Unit tests: tests/unit/test_db_session_secrets.py. No data was lost from the reproduction -- the "failed" row (Namaste Grill & Sports Bar) had already been created by the earlier 2-row test; all 26 Irving restaurants ended up seeded across the two runs.

column1: Fix: random 503s on the owner dashboard from a DB connection-pool storm + location editor missing the restaurant name
column8: Found live 2026-09-18 right after the Irving import, browsing as owner1 (23 restaurants): a DIFFERENT restaurant's location fetch failed with a bare "Request failed with status 503" on every dashboard reload, rotating randomly across restaurants -- ruled out per-row data issues (bad geocoding, timezone) by code review before finding the real cause. Root cause: portal/dashboard/page.tsx fetches every brand's locations in parallel (Promise.all across all ~23 restaurants) -- a burst of ~23 concurrent Lambda execution environments, each with its OWN DB engine/pool (module-level globals are per-container). At the prior pool_size=5/max_overflow=5, that's up to 230 simultaneous asyncpg connections against Aurora at once -- far past what a just-resumed/low-ACU Serverless v2 instance allows, so whichever requests lost that race got a bare 503 with no app-level error (connection never even reached FastAPI). Confirmed no code in app/ uses asyncio.gather/TaskGroup -- every request uses exactly one DB session, sequentially, for its whole lifetime, so a 10-connection-per-container pool was never buying anything, only multiplying the worst-case connection count by however many containers a burst spins up. Fixed: app/db/session.py's pool_size/max_overflow shrunk to 1/2 (3 connections per container, down from 10) -- not an Aurora capacity change, min_capacity=0 untouched. At realistic production scale (3-4 restaurants per owner, ~8-10 max, per direct user confirmation) this exact burst size won't recur often, but the fix is free and closes the same failure mode at any concentration of double-digit locations under one owner. Separately, also fixed in this PR: GET/POST/PATCH /locations/{id} never returned the parent brand's name (only brand_id) -- the location editor page (/portal/locations/{id}) fell back to the raw street address whenever location_name (an optional per-location label) was unset, which is every CSV-imported restaurant; user reported seeing an address instead of a restaurant name. Added brand_name to LocationOut (backend/app/schemas/location.py, app/services/location_service.py). Tests: tests/integration/test_location_brand_name_serialization.py; connection-pool fix has no direct test (would need a real concurrent-Lambda-burst integration harness, out of scope here) -- verified live instead.

column1: Follow-up fix: dashboard/admin listings still fired the full parallel fan-out after PR #101's pool-size fix -- 503s persisted
column8: PR #101's smaller per-container DB pool (1/2 vs 5/5) reduced but did not eliminate the 503s -- confirmed live: still failing, rotating restaurants, right after that fix deployed. Root cause was only half fixed: portal/dashboard/page.tsx (and admin/listings/page.tsx, same pattern) still fetch every brand's locations with a plain Promise.all across ALL restaurants -- for owner1's 23, that's still ~23 concurrent Lambda execution environments spun up at once regardless of how small each one's own pool is, and 23 x 3 connections can still exceed Aurora's real ceiling at low ACU. Fixed at the actual source: new frontend/src/lib/concurrency.ts mapWithConcurrency() caps both pages to 5 concurrent brand fetches at a time (DASHBOARD_FETCH_CONCURRENCY / LISTINGS_FETCH_CONCURRENCY) -- bounds the burst directly instead of just shrinking what each burst member asks for. At realistic production scale (3-4 restaurants/owner, ~8-10 max) this keeps dashboard loads essentially fully parallel (1-2 waves); only an outlier account like this test data's 23 restaurants gets serialized into more waves. No test added -- same reasoning as PR #101's pool-size fix, this needs a real concurrent-burst harness to verify automatically; verified live instead. column8: Found live 2026-09-18 running seed_taxonomy right after two alembic_upgrade invocations: 'got Future ... attached to a different loop'.
